title: Config
summary: git config sets your name and email, which git records as the author of every commit you make.

levels.title: Who are you?
levels.briefing: Every commit records an author, so git needs your name and email before you can commit. Without --global the setting applies to this repository only; with --global it applies to all of them.
levels.objective: Git does not know who you are yet. Set your name and email, then commit the staged file.

cheatsheet.description: Set your name for this repository
Set your email for this repository

hints: Try git commit first: the error tells you what is missing.
Set user.name and user.email with git config, then commit.
Run: git config user.name "Sam", git config user.email "sam@example.com", git commit -m "First"
levels.successMessage: Your commit now carries your name and email. git log shows them on the Author line.

levels.title: For every repository
levels.objective: Set your name and email for every repository with --global, then commit the staged file.
hints: Set both user.name and user.email that way.
Run: git config --global user.name "Sam", git config --global user.email "sam@example.com", git commit -m "First"
levels.successMessage: Global settings follow you into every repository on this computer.

levels.title: Just this repository
levels.objective: Commits in this repository should be authored by "Docs Bot". Set that name for this repository only, then commit the staged file.
hints: Leave out --global so only this repository changes.
A repository setting overrides the global one.
Run: git config user.name "Docs Bot", git commit -m "Add guide"
levels.successMessage: Repository settings win over global ones, but only inside this repository.

levels.title: Fix a typo
levels.objective: Your email is set to sam@exmaple.com by mistake. Change it to sam@example.com, then commit the staged file.
hints: Read the current value with git config user.email.
Setting a key again replaces the old value.
Run: git config --global user.email "sam@example.com", git commit -m "First"
levels.successMessage: Commits use whatever identity is set at the moment you commit.
